messages:
maria: quick heads-up — during the overnight load test in eu-west we saw low-priority inference queues fill and stay stuck while burst capacity reported as available. low latency SLOs for premium routes stayed fine, but overall throughput dropped for background jobs. attaching short dump below.

jay: interesting — was the allocator handing out GPUs to ephemeral pools first? any preemptible churn?

maria: logs show allocator favored requests with \`priority_score >= 0.8\`. but our elasticity controller used a short 30s window and aggressive prefer-burst rule, so lower-priority queues never matured their batch sizes. snippet: 

```
# simplified policy
steering:
  prefer_burst: true
  elasticity_window_secs: 30
  min_reserved_per_zone: 2
  queue_priority_fraction: {high: 0.75, normal: 0.2, low: 0.05}
cooldown: 60
```

maria: also saw scaling_score oscillate around the threshold because queued_tokens jumped in bursts, so autoscaler kept flipping node assignments.

leo: that matches something I saw last week. if the window is too short, burst decisions hog bandwidth and prevent steady-state batch buildup. we should bias steady_state for low-priority by increasing window and adding a 'maturation' requirement.

sam: propose an experiment: 
- change \`elasticity_window_secs\` to 180
- add \`min_batch_maturation: 3\` for low priority (must observe 3 consecutive windows with queue growth)
- cap prefer-burst to at most 20% of reserved headroom per zone
run for 2 hours overnight and collect p95 latency, throughput, cost.

jay: +1. also add a soft-fallback: if \`preemptible_ratio > 0.3\` then reduce prefer_burst to 0.

ops-bot: scheduled experiment: infra-experiment-124 queued for 2024-06-12T02:00Z, duration 2h, targets: eu-west1 clusters. notifications will be posted in #eng-runtime.

maria: cost note — shifting some low-priority back to sustained mode will increase steady GPU hours but should reduce small inefficient bursts that spike per-token cost. net cost estimate: +6-9% GPU hours, -12-18% tail overhead.

leo: good to capture metrics: \`queued_tokens_by_priority\`, \`batch_size_by_priority\`, \`scaling_events_per_min\`, \`p95_latency_route:<route>\`, \`cost_per_token\`. add dashboards pre/post.

sam: I'll draft the experiment runbook and rollback criteria:
- rollback if premium route p95 > 2x baseline for 15m
- rollback if error rate increases >0.5%
- stop early if sustained queue for premium routes > 60s

jay: small config wording tweak: call the new param \`steady_state_bias\` (0..1) instead of ad-hoc min_batch_maturation. default 0.25 for normal, 0.6 for low.

maria: noted. i'll update PR tonight: changes to steer controller + dashboard panels. will post the PR link once up. thanks all :thumbsup:

ops-bot: maria opened PR #1029: runtime/steering: add steady_state_bias and elasticity_window tuning — https://git.internal/redwood/pulls/1029
